claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a roughly homogeneous elemental distribution.
The as-deposited coating has a moderately sized microstructure.
A brief post-deposition anneal can promote segregation of Cr and Fe to grain boundaries in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A moderately reducing annealing atmosphere will limit premature oxidation while segregation develops.
Grain-boundary enrichment with Cr and Fe will cause rapid oxidation during elevated-temperature sliding.
The selectively segregated elements will form a fine, continuous, nanocrystalline Cr- and Fe-based oxide film along grain boundaries and the wear surface.
The resulting oxide film acts as a barrier that reduces adhesive interactions and direct metal-to-metal contact.
The resulting oxide film distributes the sliding load more uniformly.
Reduced adhesion, reduced direct contact, and more uniform load distribution will lower the coating wear rate.
Reduced adhesion, reduced direct contact, and more uniform load distribution will suppress local microscopic plastic deformation.
Compared with an untreated as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will exhibit a lower wear rate.
Compared with an untreated as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will exhibit less severe plastic flow and micro-cracking.
The untreated coating lacks pre-engineered elemental segregation.
The untreated coating forms a less protective surface oxide during high-temperature sliding than the annealed coating.
The predicted improvements should hold during sliding at 600–800°C in ambient air under moderate load and speed.
The predicted behavior may change under extreme sliding conditions or substantially different oxygen partial pressures.
